Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 71, verse 25–27:

Concerning the interpretation of His saying, ﴿Because of their sins they were drowned and then made to enter the Fire, and they found for themselves, besides Allah, no helpers﴾

By His saying, ﴿because of their sins﴾, He, exalted is He, means: because of their sins ﴿they were drowned﴾. The Arabs make "mā" (ma, a connecting particle) an addition in what is intended to carry the sense of a conditional, as one says: "Wherever you are, I will be," and "Wherever you sit, I will sit." The meaning of the statement is: because of their sins they were drowned.

Ibn Zayd used to say about this:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying, ﴿because of their sins﴾: "By their sins they were drowned," and "made to enter the Fire." The letter bā' (bi, "by") here was a separating particle in the speech of the Arabs.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, concerning His saying, ﴿Because of their sins they were drowned﴾: "By their sins they were drowned."

The reciters differed over the reading of His saying, ﴿mimmā khaṭī'ātihim﴾. The majority of the reciters of the regional centres read it ﴿mimmā khaṭī'ātihim﴾ with a hamza and a tā', while Abu 'Amr read it ﴿mimmā khaṭāyāhum﴾ with an alif and without a hamza.

Our view is that these are two well-known readings, and whichever of them the reciter reads, he is correct.

It is fa'āl from the root of "dawarān" (turning), originally "dayyār" from "dawār"; the yā' and the wāw came together, so the yā' preceded the wāw while it was quiescent, and the wāw was assimilated into it, and both became a doubled yā'. Just as it is said "al-hayy al-qayyām" from "qumtu," when it is originally "qayyām." Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 71, verse 25–27:

Concerning the interpretation of His saying, ﴿Because of their sins they were drowned and then made to enter the Fire, and they found for themselves, besides Allah, no helpers﴾

The meaning of the statement is: because of their sins they were drowned.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying, ﴿because of their sins﴾: "By their sins they were drowned," and "made to enter the Fire." The letter bā' (bi, "by") here was a separating particle in the speech of the Arabs.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, concerning His saying, ﴿Because of their sins they were drowned﴾: "By their sins they were drowned."

The reciters differed over the reading of His saying, ﴿mimmā khaṭī'ātihim﴾. The majority of the reciters of the regional centres read it ﴿mimmā khaṭī'ātihim﴾ with a hamza and a tā', while Abu 'Amr read it ﴿mimmā khaṭāyāhum﴾ with an alif and without a hamza.

Our view is that these are two well-known readings, and whichever of them the reciter reads, he is correct.

Commentary on the Words of Allah, the Exalted: "Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and will not beget except a wicked disbeliever. My Lord, forgive me and my parents and whoever enters my house in belief and the believing men and believing women. And do not increase the wrongdoers except in ruin." (71:28)

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, relating the words of Noah in his supplication against his people: "Indeed, You, O my Lord, if You leave the disbelievers alive upon the earth and do not destroy them with a punishment from You, ﴿they will mislead Your servants﴾, those who have believed in You, turning them away from Your way, ﴿and they will not beget except a wicked disbeliever﴾ in Your religion, ﴿a disbeliever﴾ in Your favor.

It is mentioned that Noah's saying this and his supplicating in this manner came after his Lord had revealed to him: ﴿that no one from your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from the disbelievers an inhabitant (dayyar)﴾. By Allah, he did not supplicate against them until revelation came to him from the heaven: ﴿that no one from your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾. At that point, the Prophet of Allah Noah supplicated against them, saying: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from the disbelievers an inhabitant. Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and will not beget except a wicked disbeliever﴾. Then he made a general supplication, saying: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and my parents and whoever enters my house in belief and the believing men and believing women﴾ ... up to His saying: ﴿ruin﴾.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, who said: Qatadah recited ﴿do not leave upon the earth from the disbelievers an inhabitant﴾, and then mentioned something similar.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and my parents﴾

He means: My Lord, pardon me, and cover over my sins and the sins of my parents. ﴿And whoever enters my house in belief﴾ means: and whoever enters my mosque and my place of prayer as a believer, meaning: one who affirms the obligation of Your command upon him.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr ibn Adam narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿whoever enters my house in belief﴾, he said: "My mosque."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Sinan Sa'id, from al-Dahhak, similarly.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and the believing men and believing women﴾

He means: and to those who affirm Your monotheism, male and female.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And do not increase the wrongdoers except in ruin﴾

He means: and do not increase the wrongdoers in themselves, through their disbelief, except in loss.

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿except in ruin (tabaran)﴾, he said: "loss."

I have already explained the meaning of the speaker's saying "tabbarat" earlier, with its evidences, and I mentioned the statements of the people of interpretation regarding it, in a way that suffices without repeating it in this place.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar said: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Mujahid, who said: "They used to beat Noah until he fainted. When he recovered, he would say: 'My Lord, forgive my people, for they do not know.'"

End of the commentary on Surat Nuh ﷺ.
